neighbours.label: ' tail' (or the second body part) closing a coordinated pair of animal body parts, as in 'mane and tail'; best guess for a pole that otherwise fires on the later member of a run of parallel items
fire: The pony's mane and tail had been braided with red ribbons.
A chestnut mare with a pale mane and tail stood by the gate.
The fox has a rusty coat with black ears and tail.
Brush the horse's mane and tail gently to remove the tangles.
The colt was dark brown, with a lighter mane and tail.
The squirrel is grey, with tufted ears and tail.
She combed the burrs out of the donkey's mane and tail.
The stallion tossed his long mane and tail in the wind.
quiet: The pony's saddle had been decorated with red ribbons.
A chestnut mare with a pale blaze stood by the gate.
The fox wagged its tail and trotted off into the hedge.
Brush the horse's coat gently to remove the dried mud.
The colt was dark brown, with a white star on his forehead.
The squirrel flicked its tail and ran up the trunk.
She pulled the burrs out of the donkey's blanket.
The stallion tossed his head and galloped into the wind.
